about: Every fitted number left in src/js. 'open' entries are retired by the part named; 'rule' entries are kept by the owner's decision. 'audit' lists files not yet read for fitted numbers. tests/test166.mjs: the lists only shrink.

entries.standsFor: a cam grade's airflow bonus; since build 260 only on rotary and two-stroke engines (a valved engine's estimates read its own integrated filling)
entries.retiredBy: ports as geometry

entries.standsFor: how a hotter cam narrows the low side of the VE bell; the bell is only on rotary and two-stroke engines
entries.retiredBy: ports as geometry

entries.standsFor: idle speed added per cam grade
entries.retiredBy: idle from overlap and residuals. Tried in build 260: Fox, Cheng & Heywood's residual correlation (SAE 931025) with a 30% dilution limit gave 1400 rpm on SPORT and no stable idle on RACE, because the model idles at 0.15 bar of manifold pressure (real 0.3-0.4) and the correlation is outside its range past ~40 deg of overlap. Needs combustion that weakens with dilution first.

entries.standsFor: torque per amp lost to saturation: one measured point (430 Nm at 953 A on the Model 3, with the flux of then; the derived flux since build 293 gives 444 Nm there), scaled with the square of the electric loading
entries.retiredBy: the lamination steel's B-H curve in the teeth and the yoke

entries.standsFor: the terminal voltage over the back-EMF at full current (one motor), the constant-power range (CPSR 4, IM_CPSR 3) with 1/w^2 beyond it, the field-weakening current as 0.7 of the inverter's, and the flux floor 0.4 in the iron loss
entries.retiredBy: the d and q inductances from the geometry, and the inverter's current and voltage limits solved on them at each speed

entries.standsFor: the stator's outside diameter as the bore over 0.67, the same for every motor. Since build 293 the teeth and yoke are sized from the flux (Pyrhonen Table 6.1) and the slot is what is left between them, so a many-pole or small motor gets deep slots and saturated teeth, or a cramped yoke, where a designer would change the diameter
entries.retiredBy: the slot's depth from the copper the current needs (Pyrhonen Table 6.2: linear current density and current density), and the outside diameter from the slot and the yoke

entries.standsFor: iron loss taken on all the iron, the rotor's included, at one flux density (B_CORE 1.5 T) and the frequency, then shared 80% stator, 20% rotor; since build 293 the teeth (2.0 T) and the yoke (1.5 T) have their own densities, which the loss does not yet read
entries.retiredBy: teeth and yoke each at their own flux density; the rotor's loss from the slot harmonics and the magnets' eddy currents

entries.standsFor: bearing friction and windage as two coefficients with no source
entries.retiredBy: bearing friction from the maker's model on the rotor's weight and the bearing's size; windage from the air gap's Taylor-Couette drag

entries.standsFor: the heat transfer coefficients of each cooling type (60 to 2500 W/m2K), the air gap's 100, the housing's contact resistance, the slot liner, the 50 mm the spray reaches, and the coolant temperatures
entries.retiredBy: channel-flow correlations on a jacket's passages and flow, the air gap's Taylor-Couette Nusselt number, cited measurements for oil spray and slot cooling

entries.standsFor: the rotor surface speed each retention survives (150 and 220 m/s), and the sleeve's 3% on inertia
entries.retiredBy: the bridges' stress from the magnets' centrifugal load against the steel's yield; the sleeve's hoop stress against the carbon's strength

entries.standsFor: each device's knee, resistance and switching energy from an unnamed module (SiC 'about a fifth'), and the output frequency ceilings 1200 and 2000 Hz
entries.retiredBy: named modules' datasheets; the ceiling as the switching frequency over the pulses a cycle needs

entries.standsFor: housing, shaft, bearings and end caps as 1.6 times the active mass; the shaft as 0.47 of the rotor's diameter
entries.retiredBy: the housing as a shell round the stator and its cooling, the shaft from the torque; or teardown masses, cited (ORNL's Leaf)

entries.standsFor: an induction motor's leakage (IM_SIGMA), resistive drop (IM_R_DROP), Carter and saturation factor (IM_KCS), constant-power range (IM_CPSR) and the cage's proportions (IM_HR, IM_RING)
